--- START OF SOURCE: 3mm.c ---
/**

/* 3mm.c: this file is part of PolyBench/C */

#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */
#include "3mm.h"


/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array(int ni, int nj, int nk, int nl, int nm,
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,NI,NK,ni,nk),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(B,NK,NJ,nk,nj),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(C,NJ,NM,nj,nm),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(D,NM,NL,nm,nl))
{
  int i, j;

  for (i = 0; i < ni; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < nk; j++)
      A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) ((i*j+1) % ni) / (5*ni);
  for (i = 0; i < nk; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < nj; j++)
      B[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) ((i*(j+1)+2) % nj) / (5*nj);
  for (i = 0; i < nj; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < nm; j++)
      C[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) (i*(j+3) % nl) / (5*nl);
  for (i = 0; i < nm; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < nl; j++)
      D[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) ((i*(j+2)+2) % nk) / (5*nk);
}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int ni, int nl,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(G,NI,NL,ni,nl))
{
  int i, j;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("G");
  for (i = 0; i < ni; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < nl; j++) {
	if ((i * ni + j) % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
	fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, G[i][j]);
    }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("G");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_3mm[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int ni, int nj, int nk, int nl, int nm,
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(E,NI,NJ,ni,nj),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,NI,NK,ni,nk),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(B,NK,NJ,nk,nj),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(F,NJ,NL,nj,nl),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(C,NJ,NM,nj,nm),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(D,NM,NL,nm,nl),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(G,NI,NL,ni,nl))
{
  int i, j, k;

#pragma scop
  /* E := A*B */
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_NI; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < _PB_NJ; j++)
      {
	E[i][j] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0);
	for (k = 0; k < _PB_NK; ++k)
	  E[i][j] += A[i][k] * B[k][j];
      }
  /* F := C*D */
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_NJ; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < _PB_NL; j++)
      {
	F[i][j] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0);
	for (k = 0; k < _PB_NM; ++k)
	  F[i][j] += C[i][k] * D[k][j];
      }
  /* G := E*F */
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_NI; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < _PB_NL; j++)
      {
	G[i][j] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0);
	for (k = 0; k < _PB_NJ; ++k)
	  G[i][j] += E[i][k] * F[k][j];
      }
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int ni = NI;
  int nj = NJ;
  int nk = NK;
  int nl = NL;
  int nm = NM;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(E, DATA_TYPE, NI, NJ, ni, nj);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(A, DATA_TYPE, NI, NK, ni, nk);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(B, DATA_TYPE, NK, NJ, nk, nj);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(F, DATA_TYPE, NJ, NL, nj, nl);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(C, DATA_TYPE, NJ, NM, nj, nm);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(D, DATA_TYPE, NM, NL, nm, nl);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(G, DATA_TYPE, NI, NL, ni, nl);

  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (ni, nj, nk, nl, nm,
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(C),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(D));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_3mm (ni, nj, nk, nl, nm,
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(E),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(F),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(C),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(D),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(G));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(ni, nl,  POLYBENCH_ARRAY(G)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(E);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(B);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(F);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(C);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(D);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(G);

  return 0;
}

--- END OF SOURCE: 3mm.c ---

--- START OF MODEL: 3mm-01 ---
domain:
    iN: dim in [0, NI)      # rows of A, E, G
    jN: dim in [0, NJ)      # cols of E, rows of B and F, reduction dim of G
    kN: dim in [0, NK)      # cols of A, rows of B
    lN: dim in [0, NL)      # cols of F and G
    mN: dim in [0, NM)      # cols of C, rows of D

data:
    # All matrices are stored row-major: last index is contiguous.
    A[iN, kN]: in    DATA_TYPE = (iN, kN) -> iN * NK + kN
    B[kN, jN]: in    DATA_TYPE = (kN, jN) -> kN * NJ + jN
    C[jN, mN]: in    DATA_TYPE = (jN, mN) -> jN * NM + mN
    D[mN, lN]: in    DATA_TYPE = (mN, lN) -> mN * NL + lN

    # E and F are internal temporaries: fully overwritten and only used
    # inside the kernel to form G.
    E[iN, jN]: temp  DATA_TYPE = (iN, jN) -> iN * NJ + jN
    F[jN, lN]: temp  DATA_TYPE = (jN, lN) -> jN * NL + lN

    # G is the only live-out array.
    G[iN, lN]: out   DATA_TYPE = (iN, lN) -> iN * NL + lN

parameters:
    # Problem sizes (compile-time constants in PolyBench, modeled as parameters here)
    NI: int
    NJ: int
    NK: int
    NL: int
    NM: int

    # Tunable block sizes; chosen so that tiles of A/B/C/D/E/F/G fit in cache.
    TI: int  # tile size along iN (rows of A/E/G)
    TJ: int  # tile size along jN (cols of E / rows of B,F / reduction dim of G)
    TK: int  # tile size along kN (inner dim of A,B)
    TL: int  # tile size along lN (cols of F,G)
    TM: int  # tile size along mN (inner dim of C,D)

    # Unrolling / vectorization parameters
    UK:  int  # unroll factor for kN in E_update
    UM:  int  # unroll factor for mN in F_update
    UJ:  int  # unroll factor for jN in G_update
    VEC: int  # SIMD vector width along the innermost (contiguous) dimension

    # Number of worker threads for parallel execution
    T: int

computation:
    #-----------------------------------------------------------
    # First GEMM:  E := A * B     (NI x NK) * (NK x NJ) -> (NI x NJ)
    #-----------------------------------------------------------

    E_init:
        for iN in [0, NI), jN in [0, NJ):
            E[iN, jN] = 0.0

    # iN-kN-jN ordering so jN (the column index) is innermost and contiguous
    # for both B[kN, jN] and E[iN, jN].
    E_update:
        for iN in [0, NI), kN in [0, NK):
            # Conceptually hoist A[iN, kN] into a scalar register here
            for jN in [0, NJ):
                E[iN, jN] += A[iN, kN] * B[kN, jN]


    #-----------------------------------------------------------
    # Second GEMM: F := C * D     (NJ x NM) * (NM x NL) -> (NJ x NL)
    #-----------------------------------------------------------

    F_init:
        for jN in [0, NJ), lN in [0, NL):
            F[jN, lN] = 0.0

    # jN-mN-lN ordering so lN (the column index) is innermost and contiguous
    # for both D[mN, lN] and F[jN, lN].
    F_update:
        for jN in [0, NJ), mN in [0, NM):
            # Conceptually hoist C[jN, mN] into a scalar register here
            for lN in [0, NL):
                F[jN, lN] += C[jN, mN] * D[mN, lN]


    #-----------------------------------------------------------
    # Third GEMM:  G := E * F     (NI x NJ) * (NJ x NL) -> (NI x NL)
    #-----------------------------------------------------------

    G_init:
        for iN in [0, NI), lN in [0, NL):
            G[iN, lN] = 0.0

    # iN-jN-lN ordering:
    #   - jN is the reduction dimension (matching NJ),
    #   - lN (columns of G and F) is innermost and contiguous.
    G_update:
        for iN in [0, NI), jN in [0, NJ):
            # Conceptually hoist E[iN, jN] into a scalar register here
            for lN in [0, NL):
                G[iN, lN] += E[iN, jN] * F[jN, lN]

optimization:
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Cache blocking (tiling)
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Tile all logical dimensions so that submatrices of A,B,C,D,E,F,G
    # stay in L2/L3 while performing the inner multiplications.
    block(iN, iNb, TI)   # iNb: tile index over rows of A/E/G
    block(jN, jNb, TJ)   # jNb: tile index over cols of E / rows of B,F
    block(kN, kNb, TK)   # kNb: tile index over inner dim of A,B
    block(lN, lNb, TL)   # lNb: tile index over cols of F,G
    block(mN, mNb, TM)   # mNb: tile index over inner dim of C,D

    # Hoist tile loops to the outermost level so that tiles are reused
    # across the innermost computations before they are evicted from cache.
    hoist(iNb)
    hoist(jNb)
    hoist(kNb)
    hoist(lNb)
    hoist(mNb)

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Loop ordering for unit-stride access
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Ensure that the innermost loop always iterates over the column
    # index (jN or lN), which is contiguous in memory.
    # These interchanges realize the iN-kN-jN, jN-mN-lN, and iN-jN-lN
    # patterns used in the computation section.
    interchange(kN, jN)  # In E_update: iN -> kN -> jN
    interchange(mN, lN)  # In F_update: jN -> mN -> lN
    interchange(jN, lN)  # In G_update: iN -> jN -> lN

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Parallelization
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Exploit outer-loop parallelism over tiles/rows.  We parallelize
    # the tile indices instead of the innermost loops to keep per-thread
    # work coarse-grained and reduce scheduling overhead.

    # E and G are naturally parallel over rows of A/E/G (iN dimension).
    parallelize(iNb)   # distribute iNb tiles across T threads for E_* and G_*

    # F is naturally parallel over rows of C/F (jN dimension).
    parallelize(jNb)   # distribute jNb tiles across T threads for F_*

    # E and F computations are completely independent; they can run in
    # parallel "sections" prior to starting G.
    # (Non-standard directive: expresses two independent parallel tasks.)
    parallel_sections({E_init, E_update}, {F_init, F_update})

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Vectorization and unrolling
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Vectorize along the innermost (contiguous) column dimension and
    # unroll reductions to increase ILP and aid the compiler.
    vectorize(jN, VEC)  # innermost loop of E_update
    vectorize(lN, VEC)  # innermost loops of F_update and G_update

    unroll(kN, UK)      # unroll reduction over kN in E_update
    unroll(mN, UM)      # unroll reduction over mN in F_update
    unroll(jN, UJ)      # unroll reduction over jN in G_update

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. Scalar replacement / register blocking
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Non-standard directive:
    #   scalar_replace(S) means: for each access pattern in S that is
    #   invariant in the innermost loop, keep it in a scalar register.
    #
    # Here we keep:
    #   - A[iN, kN] across the jN-loop in E_update,
    #   - C[jN, mN] across the lN-loop in F_update,
    #   - E[iN, jN] across the lN-loop in G_update.
    scalar_replace({A[iN, kN], C[jN, mN], E[iN, jN]})

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 6. Optional: software prefetching of next tiles
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Non-standard hint:
    # Prefetch upcoming tiles of B, D, and F one tile ahead along the
    # kNb/mNb/jNb dimensions to overlap memory latency with computation.
    prefetch({B, D, F}, distance = one_tile_ahead)
--- END OF MODEL: 3mm-01 ---

--- START OF MODEL: 3mm-02 ---
domain:
    # Dimensions correspond to the problem sizes (matrix extents)
    i: dim in [0, NI)   # rows of A, E, G
    j: dim in [0, NJ)   # cols of B, E; rows of C, F; reduction dim in G
    k: dim in [0, NK)   # shared dim of A (cols) and B (rows)
    l: dim in [0, NL)   # cols of D, F, G
    m: dim in [0, NM)   # shared dim of C (cols) and D (rows)

data:
    # Left operands of GEMMs: row-major
    A[i, k]: in   DATA_TYPE = (i, k) -> i * NK + k        # NI x NK
    C[j, m]: in   DATA_TYPE = (j, m) -> j * NM + m        # NJ x NM

    # Right operands of GEMMs: column-major
    # (so the reduction index is contiguous for dot products)
    B[k, j]: in   DATA_TYPE = (k, j) -> j * NK + k        # NK x NJ, column-major
    D[m, l]: in   DATA_TYPE = (m, l) -> l * NM + m        # NM x NL, column-major

    # Intermediates
    E[i, j]: tmp  DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * NJ + j        # NI x NJ, row-major
    F[j, l]: tmp  DATA_TYPE = (j, l) -> l * NJ + j        # NJ x NL, column-major

    # Final result
    G[i, l]: out  DATA_TYPE = (i, l) -> i * NL + l        # NI x NL, row-major

parameters:
    # Problem sizes (modeled as parameters, but compile-time constants in PolyBench)
    NI: int
    NJ: int
    NK: int
    NL: int
    NM: int

    # Tunable tile sizes (chosen for cache hierarchy of the target system)
    TI_E: int  # tile size for i in E = A * B
    TJ_E: int  # tile size for j in E = A * B
    TK_E: int  # tile size for k in E = A * B

    TJ_F: int  # tile size for j in F = C * D
    TL_F: int  # tile size for l in F = C * D
    TM_F: int  # tile size for m in F = C * D

    TI_G: int  # tile size for i in G = E * F
    TL_G: int  # tile size for l in G = E * F
    TJ_G: int  # tile size for j (reduction dim) in G = E * F

    VEC:  int  # SIMD vector length in elements (e.g., 4/8 for double; 8/16 for float)

computation:
    # Phase 1: E := A * B   (NI x NJ  =  NI x NK  *  NK x NJ)
    E_phase:
        for i, j:
            E[i, j] = sum(k, A[i, k] * B[k, j])

    # Phase 2: F := C * D   (NJ x NL  =  NJ x NM  *  NM x NL)
    F_phase:
        for j, l:
            F[j, l] = sum(m, C[j, m] * D[m, l])

    # Phase 3: G := E * F   (NI x NL  =  NI x NJ  *  NJ x NL)
    G_phase:
        for i, l:
            G[i, l] = sum(j, E[i, j] * F[j, l])

dependencies:
    # E and F are independent; G depends on both.
    E_phase -> G_phase
    F_phase -> G_phase

optimization:
    # ==========================================================
    # General strategy
    # ==========================================================
    # - Keep the reduction index innermost in each GEMM, so that:
    #     * left operand uses row-major layout with contiguous access
    #     * right operand uses column-major layout with contiguous access
    #   This makes the innermost loop a vectorizable dot product.
    # - Tile the (row, col, reduction) dimensions to improve cache reuse.
    # - Use outer tiles for parallelization across cores.
    # - Use scalar accumulators per output element within tiles to minimize
    #   memory traffic (read/write E, F, G only once per tile).
    # - Optional packing for B, D, F tiles keeps packed buffers small enough
    #   that added memory is well below +50% of the original footprint.

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # Phase 1: E = A * B
    # Loop shape after transformation:
    #
    # for iE in 0..NI step TI_E         # tiled, parallel
    #   for jE in 0..NJ step TJ_E
    #     for kE in 0..NK step TK_E
    #       for i in iE .. min(iE+TI_E, NI)
    #         for j in jE .. min(jE+TJ_E, NJ)
    #           acc = (kE == 0 ? 0 : E[i,j])
    #           for k in kE .. min(kE+TK_E, NK)   # contiguous A[i,k] and B[k,j]
    #             acc += A[i,k] * B[k,j]
    #           E[i,j] = acc
    #
    block(i, iE, TI_E)             # tile over rows of A/E
    block(j, jE, TJ_E)             # tile over cols of B/E
    block(k, kE, TK_E)             # tile over reduction dimension
    hoist(iE)                      # make tile loops outermost: iE, jE, kE
    hoist(jE)
    hoist(kE)
    parallelize(iE)                # distribute row-tiles across threads
    vectorize(k, VEC)              # vectorize dot product over k
    unroll(k, 4)                   # unroll for ILP within a SIMD chunk

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # Phase 2: F = C * D
    # Similar tiling over (j, l, m), j-tiles in parallel.
    #
    # for jF in 0..NJ step TJ_F      # tiled, parallel (rows of C/F)
    #   for lF in 0..NL step TL_F
    #     for mF in 0..NM step TM_F
    #       for j in jF .. min(jF+TJ_F, NJ)
    #         for l in lF .. min(lF+TL_F, NL)
    #           acc = (mF == 0 ? 0 : F[j,l]
    #           for m in mF .. min(mF+TM_F, NM)   # contiguous C[j,m], D[m,l]
    #             acc += C[j,m] * D[m,l]
    #           F[j,l] = acc
    #
    block(j, jF, TJ_F)             # tile rows of C/F
    block(l, lF, TL_F)             # tile cols of D/F
    block(m, mF, TM_F)             # tile reduction dimension
    hoist(jF)
    hoist(lF)
    hoist(mF)
    parallelize(jF)                # distribute row-tiles across threads
    vectorize(m, VEC)              # vectorize dot product over m
    unroll(m, 4)

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # Phase 3: G = E * F
    # Tiling and parallelization over (i, l, j). j is reduction dim.
    #
    # for iG in 0..NI step TI_G      # tiled, parallel (rows of E/G)
    #   for lG in 0..NL step TL_G
    #     for jG in 0..NJ step TJ_G
    #       for i in iG .. min(iG+TI_G, NI)
    #         for l in lG .. min(lG+TL_G, NL)
    #           acc = (jG == 0 ? 0 : G[i,l])
    #           for j in jG .. min(jG+TJ_G, NJ)   # contiguous E[i,j], F[j,l]
    #             acc += E[i,j] * F[j,l]
    #           G[i,l] = acc
    #
    block(i, iG, TI_G)             # tile rows of E/G
    block(l, lG, TL_G)             # tile cols of F/G
    block(j, jG, TJ_G)             # tile reduction dimension
    hoist(iG)
    hoist(lG)
    hoist(jG)
    parallelize(iG)                # distribute row-tiles across threads
    vectorize(j, VEC)              # vectorize dot product over j
    unroll(j, 4)

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # Data layout and packing
    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # The data section already specifies B, D, and F as column-major, so an
    # implementation should either:
    #   - allocate them directly in that layout, or
    #   - pack tiles on the fly into small contiguous buffers.
    #
    # Below are non-standard directives describing per-tile packing.
    #
    # pack(M, [rdim, cdim], [Rtile, Ctile]) means:
    #   For each (Rtile, Ctile) tile of matrix M, allocate a temporary buffer
    #   of size (tile_size(rdim) x tile_size(cdim)) and copy M's elements into
    #   a layout where 'rdim' is contiguous. Buffers are reused across tiles,
    #   and their total size is O(T* T) per thread, far below 50% overhead.
    #
    pack(B, [k, j], [kE, jE])      # pack B tiles for better use of L1/L2
    pack(D, [m, l], [mF, lF])      # similarly for D
    pack(F, [j, l], [jG, lG])      # optional: pack F tiles for phase 3

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # Task parallelism between independent phases
    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # E_phase and F_phase are independent; they can be run as separate tasks
    # sharing a thread pool. G_phase starts after both complete.
    #
    # Non-standard directives:
    #   task_parallel(L1, L2, ...) : run labeled computations as concurrent tasks
    #   task_sync(L)               : L can start only after all prior tasks finish
    #
    task_parallel(E_phase, F_phase)
    task_sync(G_phase)
--- END OF MODEL: 3mm-02 ---

--- START OF MODEL: 3mm-03 ---
domain:
    # Matrix index spaces
    i: dim in [0, NI)   # rows of A, E, G
    j: dim in [0, NJ)   # cols of E, rows of C,F and reduction dim in G
    k: dim in [0, NK)   # cols of A, rows of B (reduction for E)
    l: dim in [0, NL)   # cols of F, G
    m: dim in [0, NM)   # cols of C, rows of D (reduction for F)

data:
    # All arrays are row-major: element (r,c) is stored at base + r * (#cols) + c.

    A[i, k]: in DATA_TYPE
        = (i, k) -> i * NK + k          # A is NI x NK

    B[k, j]: in DATA_TYPE
        = (k, j) -> k * NJ + j          # B is NK x NJ

    C[j, m]: in DATA_TYPE
        = (j, m) -> j * NM + m          # C is NJ x NM

    D[m, l]: in DATA_TYPE
        = (m, l) -> m * NL + l          # D is NM x NL

    E[i, j]: temp DATA_TYPE
        = (i, j) -> i * NJ + j          # E is NI x NJ, intermediate A*B

    F[j, l]: temp DATA_TYPE
        = (j, l) -> j * NL + l          # F is NJ x NL, intermediate C*D

    G[i, l]: out DATA_TYPE
        = (i, l) -> i * NL + l          # G is NI x NL, final result

    TJ: int  # tile size in j (cols of E / rows of C,F / reduction of G)

    TL: int  # tile size in l (cols of F,G)
    TM: int  # tile size in m (reduction for F)

    # E := A * B   (NI x NK) * (NK x NJ) -> (NI x NJ)

    # accumulator per (i,j) element and writes back once.

        for j, l:

    # each other and can be computed in parallel.

    for i in [0, NI), l in [0, NL), j in [0, NJ):

optimization:
    #--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Cache blocking (tiling) on all spatial and reduction dimensions
    #--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    # in-tile loop over D, with tile size S.

    # Global tiling of index spaces, shared across all three GEMMs.
    block(i, I, TI)    # rows of A,E,G
    block(j, J, TJ)    # cols of E / rows of C,F / reduction dim of G

    block(l, L, TL)    # cols of F,G
    block(m, M, TM)    # reduction for F

    # 2. Loop ordering per matrix multiplication
    #--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    #   - iterate innermost over a contiguous memory dimension (j or l),
    #   - hoist a single A/C/E element into a scalar and reuse it across that
    #     inner loop, minimizing loads and enabling SIMD.
    #
    # We introduce a "schedule" directive:
    #   schedule(LABEL, [LOOP_VARS...])
    # which prescribes the loop-nest order (from outermost to innermost)
    # for the computation labeled LABEL, after tiling.
    #
    # For each tiled dimension D with tile index TD, the effective loops are:
    #   for TD in tiles:
    #     for D in TD-tile:
    # and "schedule" places both TD and D in the desired order.

    # E = A * B
    #   Target scalar structure (ignoring tiles):
    #     for i
    #       for k
    #         aik = A[i,k]
    #         for j    # j contiguous: accesses E[i,*], B[k,*] row-wise
    #           E[i,j] += aik * B[k,j]
    #
    #   Tiled/scheduled order: I, K, J, i, k, j
    schedule(E_def, [I, K, J, i, k, j])

    # F = C * D
    #   Target scalar structure:
    #     for j
    #       for m
    #         cjm = C[j,m]
    #         for l    # l contiguous: accesses F[j,*], D[m,*] row-wise
    #           F[j,l] += cjm * D[m,l]
    #
    #   Tiled/scheduled order: J, M, L, j, m, l
    schedule(F_def, [J, M, L, j, m, l])

    # G = E * F
    #   Target scalar structure:
    #     for i
    #       for j
    #         eij = E[i,j]
    #         for l    # l contiguous: accesses G[i,*], F[j,*] row-wise
    #           G[i,l] += eij * F[j,l]
    #
    #   Tiled/scheduled order: I, J, L, i, j, l
    schedule(G_def, [I, J, L, i, j, l])

    #--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Parallelization
    #--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Thread-level parallelism over outer tile loops. The machine has many cores,
    # so we use coarse-grain tiles as parallel units.

    # Parallelize E and G over tiles of rows (I). This distributes rows of E and G.
    parallelize(I)

    # Parallelize F over tiles of its outer dimension (J: rows of C,F).
    parallelize(J)

    # Optional task-level parallelism between the independent GEMMs E and F.
    # We introduce:
    #   parallel_sections(L1, L2)

    # dependent computations (here: G_def).
    parallel_sections(E_def, F_def)

    #--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Vectorization and unrolling
    #--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Vectorize along the innermost contiguous dimensions to exploit SIMD:
    #   - j for E (updates along rows of E and B),
    #   - l for F (updates along rows of F and D),
    #   - l for G (updates along rows of G and F).

    vectorize(j, VEC_J)   # inner loop of E
    vectorize(l, VEC_L)   # inner loops of F and G

    # Unroll reduction loops to increase ILP and better hide load latency.
    unroll(k, UK)         # unroll k-reduction in E
    unroll(m, UM)         # unroll m-reduction in F

    #--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. Hoisting of tile loops and scalar temporaries
    #--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Hoist tile loops to outermost position for each GEMM to maximize reuse of
    # tiles in cache and to make parallelization across tiles effective.

    hoist(I)
    hoist(J)
    hoist(K)
    hoist(L)
    hoist(M)

    # Within each innermost non-tiled nest, use scalar temporaries:
    #   - In E_def: aik = A[i,k], reused across all j in the tile.
    #   - In F_def: cjm = C[j,m], reused across all l in the tile.
    #   - In G_def: eij = E[i,j], reused across all l in the tile.
    #
    # These are implicit in the schedules above and reduce memory traffic by
    # turning repeated loads into register reuse, while keeping the arithmetic
    # identical (up to floating-point re-association permitted by blocking).

    B[k, j]: in DATA_TYPE
        = (k, j) -> k * NJ + j           # NK x NJ, row-major

    C[j, m]: in DATA_TYPE
        = (j, m) -> j * NM + m           # NJ x NM, row-major

    D[m, l]: in DATA_TYPE
        = (m, l) -> m * NL + l           # NM x NL, row-major

    # In the baseline code they are fully materialized; in the optimized
    # model they may be partially or not materialized at all (see fusion

    NJ: int

    NM: int
    NL: int

    TJ: int  # tile size along j (cols of B/E, rows of C/F)
    TK: int  # tile size along k (reduction for E)
    TM: int  # tile size along m (reduction for F)
    TL: int  # tile size along l (cols of D/F/G)

    VEC_L: int  # vector width when iterating l-contiguous data

    UNROLL_M: int  # for m in F

computation:
    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. E := A * B   (NI x NK) * (NK x NJ) -> (NI x NJ)
    #     E[i, j] = sum_k A[i, k] * B[k, j]
    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    E_gemm:
        for i, j:
            E[i, j] = sum(k, A[i, k] * B[k, j])

    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. F := C * D   (NJ x NM) * (NM x NL) -> (NJ x NL)
    #     F[j, l] = sum_m C[j, m] * D[m, l]
    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    F_gemm:
        for j, l:
            F[j, l] = sum(m, C[j, m] * D[m, l])

    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. G := E * F   (NI x NJ) * (NJ x NL) -> (NI x NL)
    #     G[i, l] = sum_j E[i, j] * F[j, l]
    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    G_gemm:
        for i, l:
            G[i, l] = sum(j, E[i, j] * F[j, l])

dependencies:
    # E_gemm and F_gemm are completely independent.
    # G_gemm depends on the final values of both E and F.
    E_gemm -> G_gemm
    F_gemm -> G_gemm

optimization:
    #==================================================================
    # Cache blocking / tiling
    #==================================================================
    # Block all major dimensions to improve cache reuse.
    # The same symbolic tile sizes are reused across the three GEMMs.
    # This is semantically equivalent to the original loops; it only
    # changes the order of associative+commutative floating-point sums.

    # Tile "row" dimensions
    block(i, I, TI)   # I: tile index over rows of A, E, G
    block(j, J, TJ)   # J: tile index over NJ (cols of B/E, rows of C/F)
    block(l, L, TL)   # L: tile index over cols of D/F/G

    # Tile reduction dimensions
    block(k, K, TK)   # K: tile index over NK reduction in E_gemm
    block(m, M, TM)   # M: tile index over NM reduction in F_gemm

    # After blocking, the conceptual structure is:
    #
    #   E_gemm:
    #     for I in [0, NI) step TI
    #       for K in [0, NK) step TK
    #         for J in [0, NJ) step TJ
    #           for i in I-tile, k in K-tile, j in J-tile
    #             E[i, j] += A[i, k] * B[k, j]
    #
    #   F_gemm:
    #     for J in [0, NJ) step TJ
    #       for M in [0, NM) step TM
    #         for L in [0, NL) step TL
    #           for j in J-tile, m in M-tile, l in L-tile
    #             F[j, l] += C[j, m] * D[m, l]
    #
    #   G_gemm:
    #     for I in [0, NI) step TI
    #       for J in [0, NJ) step TJ
    #         for L in [0, NL) step TL
    #           for i in I-tile, j in J-tile, l in L-tile
    #             G[i, l] += E[i, j] * F[j, l]

    #==================================================================
    # Loop reordering for unit-stride access
    #==================================================================
    # Reorder loops inside each tile to maximize contiguous accesses.
    # Idea:
    #   - In E_gemm, use order (i, k, j):
    #       * A[i, k] traverses k contiguously (row of A).
    #       * B[k, j] traverses j contiguously (row of B).
    #       * E[i, j] traverses j contiguously (row of E).
    #
    #   - In F_gemm, use order (j, m, l):
    #       * C[j, m] traverses m contiguously (row of C).
    #       * D[m, l] traverses l contiguously (row of D).
    #       * F[j, l] traverses l contiguously (row of F).
    #
    #   - In G_gemm, use order (i, j, l):
    #       * E[i, j] traverses j contiguously (row of E).
    #       * F[j, l] traverses l contiguously (row of F).
    #       * G[i, l] traverses l contiguously (row of G).

    # These are implemented via loop interchange directives:
    interchange(j, k)   # in E_gemm: swap j and k to realize (i, k, j)
    interchange(l, m)   # in F_gemm: swap l and m to realize (j, m, l)
    interchange(l, j)   # in G_gemm: swap inner (j, l) to realize (i, j, l)

    #==================================================================
    # Use multi-core parallelism on the outer tiles; tile sizes TI, TJ, TL

    block(i, I_par, TI)
    parallelize(I_par)   # distribute I-tiles of E_gemm across threads

    # F_gemm: different J-tiles touch disjoint rows of F, so can be parallel.
    block(j, J_par, TJ)
    parallelize(J_par)   # distribute J-tiles of F_gemm across threads

    # G_gemm: again, rows of G are independent; parallelize over I-tiles.
    block(i, I_par_G, TI)

    #==================================================================

    unroll(m, UNROLL_M)   # reduction over m in F_gemm
    unroll(j, UNROLL_J)   # reduction over j in G_gemm

    #==================================================================
    # Scalar replacement / register reuse
    #==================================================================
    # Within the reordered loops, hoist frequently used values into
    # scalars to minimize memory traffic. Conceptually:
    #
    #   - E_gemm inner kernel (within a tile):
    #       for i in I, for k in K:
    #           a_ik = A[i, k]              # hoist A[i,k]
    #           for j in J:

    #

    #           for l in L:
    #               F[j, l] += c_jm * D[m, l]
    #
    #   - G_gemm inner kernel:
    #       for i in I, for j in J:
    #           e_ij = E[i, j]              # hoist E[i,j]
    #           for l in L:
    #               G[i, l] += e_ij * F[j, l]
    #

    # replacement automatically once loop orders are as above.

    #==================================================================
    # Optional fusion to avoid fully materializing E
    #==================================================================
    # Since the program only observes G, E and F are intermediates.
    # It is legal (under the C "as-if" rule) to change the way they
    # are computed as long as G is unchanged.

    # The most profitable fusion here is to avoid writing/reading E:
    #
    #   1. Compute F as before (F_gemm).
    #   2. Fuse E_gemm into G_gemm along the shared dimension j:

    #   This preserves G exactly and reduces memory traffic by removing
    #   the large NI x NJ intermediate E.
    #

    #
    #fuse(E_gemm, G_gemm, along = j)

    #  #     of e_ij inside G's accumulation over j.
    #  #   - Maintain all blocking, parallelization and vectorization

    #  #   - Does not increase asymptotic flop count and reduces memory

parameters:

computation:

    #     for j in 0..NJ-1
    #       E[i][j] = 0;
    #       for k in 0..NK-1

optimization:

    # - All sums (sum(...)) are implemented as scalar reductions in

    # - Blocking (tiling) is applied so that each inner kernel works on
    #   submatrices that fit in cache, increasing temporal locality.
    # - Vectorization targets the innermost, contiguous dimension in

    #========================

    #   for i, j: E[i,j] = sum_k A[i,k] * B[k,j]
    # We transform loops to an i-k-j ordering with 3D blocking:
    #   for I_E in tiles of i
    #     for K_E in tiles of k
    #       for J_E in tiles of j
    #         for i inside I_E
    #           for k inside K_E

    #             for j inside J_E
    #               E[i,j] += a_ik * B[k,j]
    #

    #   - reuses A[i,k] across a block of columns j (register reuse)
    #   - accesses B[k,*] and E[i,*] contiguously along j
    #   - keeps each thread's writes to E disjoint when parallelizing over I_E.

    block(j, J_E, TJ_E)   # outer tile index J_E, inner j

#include <polybench.h>

/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array(int ni, int nj, int nk, int nl, int nm,
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,NI,NK,ni,nk),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(B,NK,NJ,nk,nj),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(C,NJ,NM,nj,nm),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(D,NM,NL,nm,nl))
{
  int i, j;

  for (i = 0; i < ni; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < nk; j++)
      A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) ((i*j+1) % ni) / (5*ni);
  for (i = 0; i < nk; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < nj; j++)
      B[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) ((i*(j+1)+2) % nj) / (5*nj);
  for (i = 0; i < nj; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < nm; j++)
      C[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) (i*(j+3) % nl) / (5*nl);
  for (i = 0; i < nm; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < nl; j++)
      D[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) ((i*(j+2)+2) % nk) / (5*nk);
}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int ni, int nl,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(G,NI,NL,ni,nl))
{
  int i, j;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("G");
  for (i = 0; i < ni; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < nl; j++) {
	if ((i * ni + j) % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
	fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, G[i][j]);
    }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("G");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_3mm[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int ni, int nj, int nk, int nl, int nm,
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(E,NI,NJ,ni,nj),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,NI,NK,ni,nk),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(B,NK,NJ,nk,nj),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(F,NJ,NL,nj,nl),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(C,NJ,NM,nj,nm),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(D,NM,NL,nm,nl),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(G,NI,NL,ni,nl))
{
  int i, j, k;

#pragma scop
  /* E := A*B */
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_NI; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < _PB_NJ; j++)
      {
	E[i][j] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0);
	for (k = 0; k < _PB_NK; ++k)
	  E[i][j] += A[i][k] * B[k][j];
      }
  /* F := C*D */
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_NJ; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < _PB_NL; j++)
      {
	F[i][j] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0);
	for (k = 0; k < _PB_NM; ++k)
	  F[i][j] += C[i][k] * D[k][j];
      }
  /* G := E*F */
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_NI; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < _PB_NL; j++)
      {
	G[i][j] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0);
	for (k = 0; k < _PB_NJ; ++k)
	  G[i][j] += E[i][k] * F[k][j];
      }
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int ni = NI;
  int nj = NJ;
  int nk = NK;
  int nl = NL;
  int nm = NM;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(E, DATA_TYPE, NI, NJ, ni, nj);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(A, DATA_TYPE, NI, NK, ni, nk);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(B, DATA_TYPE, NK, NJ, nk, nj);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(F, DATA_TYPE, NJ, NL, nj, nl);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(C, DATA_TYPE, NJ, NM, nj, nm);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(D, DATA_TYPE, NM, NL, nm, nl);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(G, DATA_TYPE, NI, NL, ni, nl);

  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (ni, nj, nk, nl, nm,
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(C),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(D));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_3mm (ni, nj, nk, nl, nm,
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(E),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(F),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(C),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(D),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(G));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(ni, nl,  POLYBENCH_ARRAY(G)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(E);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(B);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(F);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(C);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(D);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(G);

  return 0;
}

    block(j, jF, TJ_F)             # tile rows of C/F
    block(l, lF, TL_F)             # tile cols of D/F
    block(m, mF, TM_F)             # tile reduction dimension
    hoist(jF)
    hoist(lF)
    hoist(mF)
    parallelize(jF)                # distribute row-tiles across threads
    vectorize(m, VEC)              # vectorize dot product over m
    unroll(m, 4)

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # Phase 3: G = E * F
    # Tiling and parallelization over (i, l, j). j is reduction dim.
    #
    # for iG in 0..NI step TI_G      # tiled, parallel (rows of E/G)
    #   for lG in 0..NL step TL_G
    #     for jG in 0..NJ step TJ_G
    #       for i in iG .. min(iG+TI_G, NI)
    #         for l in lG .. min(lG+TL_G, NL)
    #           acc = (jG == 0 ? 0 : G[i,l])
    #           for j in jG .. min(jG+TJ_G, NJ)   # contiguous E[i,j], F[j,l]
    #             acc += E[i,j] * F[j,l]
    #           G[i,l] = acc
    #
    block(i, iG, TI_G)             # tile rows of E/G
    block(l, lG, TL_G)             # tile cols of F/G
    block(j, jG, TJ_G)             # tile reduction dimension
    hoist(iG)
    hoist(lG)
    hoist(jG)
    parallelize(iG)                # distribute row-tiles across threads
    vectorize(j, VEC)              # vectorize dot product over j
    unroll(j, 4)

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # Data layout and packing
    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # The data section already specifies B, D, and F as column-major, so an
    # implementation should either:
    #   - allocate them directly in that layout, or
    #   - pack tiles on the fly into small contiguous buffers.
    #
    # Below are non-standard directives describing per-tile packing.
    #
    # pack(M, [rdim, cdim], [Rtile, Ctile]) means:
    #   For each (Rtile, Ctile) tile of matrix M, allocate a temporary buffer
    #   of size (tile_size(rdim) x tile_size(cdim)) and copy M's elements into
    #   a layout where 'rdim' is contiguous. Buffers are reused across tiles,
    #   and their total size is O(T* T) per thread, far below 50% overhead.
    #
    pack(B, [k, j], [kE, jE])      # pack B tiles for better use of L1/L2
    pack(D, [m, l], [mF, lF])      # similarly for D
    pack(F, [j, l], [jG, lG])      # optional: pack F tiles for phase 3

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # Task parallelism between independent phases
    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # E_phase and F_phase are independent; they can be run as separate tasks
    # sharing a thread pool. G_phase starts after both complete.
    #
    # Non-standard directives:
    #   task_parallel(L1, L2, ...) : run labeled computations as concurrent tasks
    #   task_sync(L)               : L can start only after all prior tasks finish
    #
    task_parallel(E_phase, F_phase)
    task_sync(G_phase)

domain:
    # Matrix index spaces
    i: dim in [0, NI)   # rows of A, E, G
    j: dim in [0, NJ)   # cols of E, rows of C,F and reduction dim in G
    k: dim in [0, NK)   # cols of A, rows of B (reduction for E)
    l: dim in [0, NL)   # cols of F, G
    m: dim in [0, NM)   # cols of C, rows of D (reduction for F)

data:
    # All arrays are row-major: element (r,c) is stored at base + r * (#cols) + c.

    A[i, k]: in DATA_TYPE
        = (i, k) -> i * NK + k          # A is NI x NK

    B[k, j]: in DATA_TYPE
        = (k, j) -> k * NJ + j          # B is NK x NJ

    C[j, m]: in DATA_TYPE
        = (j, m) -> j * NM + m          # C is NJ x NM

    D[m, l]: in DATA_TYPE
        = (m, l) -> m * NL + l          # D is NM x NL

    E[i, j]: temp DATA_TYPE
        = (i, j) -> i * NJ + j          # E is NI x NJ, intermediate A*B

    F[j, l]: temp DATA_TYPE
        = (j, l) -> j * NL + l          # F is NJ x NL, intermediate C*D

    G[i, l]: out DATA_TYPE
        = (i, l) -> i * NL + l          # G is NI x NL, final result


parameters:
    # Tunable tile sizes (compile-time or run-time constants).
    TI: int  # tile size in i (rows of A,E,G)
    TJ: int  # tile size in j (cols of E / rows of C,F / reduction of G)
    TK: int  # tile size in k (reduction for E)
    TL: int  # tile size in l (cols of F,G)
    TM: int  # tile size in m (reduction for F)

    # Vectorization and unrolling factors (hardware-dependent).
    VEC_J: int  # SIMD width for j-contiguous updates (E and G)
    VEC_L: int  # SIMD width for l-contiguous updates (F and G)
    UK:    int  # unroll factor for k-reduction (E)
    UM:    int  # unroll factor for m-reduction (F)


computation:
    # E := A * B   (NI x NK) * (NK x NJ) -> (NI x NJ)
    # Implemented as the mathematical matrix product; scalar code uses an
    # accumulator per (i,j) element and writes back once.
    E_def:
        for i, j:
            E[i, j] = sum(k, A[i, k] * B[k, j])

    # F := C * D   (NJ x NM) * (NM x NL) -> (NJ x NL)
    F_def:
        for j, l:
            F[j, l] = sum(m, C[j, m] * D[m, l])

    # G := E * F   (NI x NJ) * (NJ x NL) -> (NI x NL)
    G_def:
        for i, l:
            G[i, l] = sum(j, E[i, j] * F[j, l])


dependencies:
    # G depends on the full results of E and F; E and F are independent of
    # each other and can be computed in parallel.

    # Each G[i,l] depends on all E[i,j] for j in [0,NJ) and all F[j,l].
    for i in [0, NI), l in [0, NL), j in [0, NJ):
        E_def(i, j) -> G_def(i, l)

    for i in [0, NI), l in [0, NL), j in [0, NJ):
        F_def(j, l) -> G_def(i, l)

    # No dependence between E_def and F_def:
    #   E_def(i,j) and F_def(j',l') are mutually independent for all indices.


optimization:
    #--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Cache blocking (tiling) on all spatial and reduction dimensions
    #--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # block(D, TD, S) splits loop over D into an outer tile loop TD and an inner
    # in-tile loop over D, with tile size S.

    # Global tiling of index spaces, shared across all three GEMMs.
    block(i, I, TI)    # rows of A,E,G
    block(j, J, TJ)    # cols of E / rows of C,F / reduction dim of G
    block(k, K, TK)    # reduction for E
    block(l, L, TL)    # cols of F,G
    block(m, M, TM)    # reduction for F

    #--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Loop ordering per matrix multiplication
    #--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # We choose loop orders that:
    #   - iterate innermost over a contiguous memory dimension (j or l),
    #   - hoist a single A/C/E element into a scalar and reuse it across that
    #     inner loop, minimizing loads and enabling SIMD.
    #
    # We introduce a "schedule" directive:
    #   schedule(LABEL, [LOOP_VARS...])
    # which prescribes the loop-nest order (from outermost to innermost)
    # for the computation labeled LABEL, after tiling.
    #
    # For each tiled dimension D with tile index TD, the effective loops are:
    #   for TD in tiles:
    #     for D in TD-tile:
    # and "schedule" places both TD and D in the desired order.

    # E = A * B
    #   Target scalar structure (ignoring tiles):
    #     for i
    #       for k
    #         aik = A[i,k]
    #         for j    # j contiguous: accesses E[i,*], B[k,*] row-wise
    #           E[i,j] += aik * B[k,j]
    #
    #   Tiled/scheduled order: I, K, J, i, k, j
    schedule(E_def, [I, K, J, i, k, j])

    # F = C * D
    #   Target scalar structure:
    #     for j
    #       for m
    #         cjm = C[j,m]
    #         for l    # l contiguous: accesses F[j,*], D[m,*] row-wise
    #           F[j,l] += cjm * D[m,l]
    #
    #   Tiled/scheduled order: J, M, L, j, m, l
    schedule(F_def, [J, M, L, j, m, l])

    # G = E * F
    #   Target scalar structure:
    #     for i
    #       for j
    #         eij = E[i,j]
    #         for l    # l contiguous: accesses G[i,*], F[j,*] row-wise
    #           G[i,l] += eij * F[j,l]
    #
    #   Tiled/scheduled order: I, J, L, i, j, l
    schedule(G_def, [I, J, L, i, j, l])

    #--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Parallelization
    #--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Thread-level parallelism over outer tile loops. The machine has many cores,
    # so we use coarse-grain tiles as parallel units.

    # Parallelize E and G over tiles of rows (I). This distributes rows of E and G.
    parallelize(I)

    # Parallelize F over tiles of its outer dimension (J: rows of C,F).
    parallelize(J)

    # Optional task-level parallelism between the independent GEMMs E and F.
    # We introduce:
    #   parallel_sections(L1, L2)
    # meaning that the computations labeled L1 and L2 run concurrently in
    # different threads, with an implicit barrier before any use of later
    # dependent computations (here: G_def).
    parallel_sections(E_def, F_def)

    #--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Vectorization and unrolling
    #--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Vectorize along the innermost contiguous dimensions to exploit SIMD:
    #   - j for E (updates along rows of E and B),
    #   - l for F (updates along rows of F and D),
    #   - l for G (updates along rows of G and F).

    vectorize(j, VEC_J)   # inner loop of E
    vectorize(l, VEC_L)   # inner loops of F and G

    # Unroll reduction loops to increase ILP and better hide load latency.
    unroll(k, UK)         # unroll k-reduction in E
    unroll(m, UM)         # unroll m-reduction in F

    #--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. Hoisting of tile loops and scalar temporaries
    #--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Hoist tile loops to outermost position for each GEMM to maximize reuse of
    # tiles in cache and to make parallelization across tiles effective.

    hoist(I)
    hoist(J)
    hoist(K)
    hoist(L)
    hoist(M)

    # Within each innermost non-tiled nest, use scalar temporaries:
    #   - In E_def: aik = A[i,k], reused across all j in the tile.
    #   - In F_def: cjm = C[j,m], reused across all l in the tile.
    #   - In G_def: eij = E[i,j], reused across all l in the tile.
    #
    # These are implicit in the schedules above and reduce memory traffic by
    # turning repeated loads into register reuse, while keeping the arithmetic
    # identical (up to floating-point re-association permitted by blocking).
--- END OF MODEL: 3mm-03 ---

domain:
    # Matrix dimensions
    i: dim in [0, NI)   # rows of A, E, G
    j: dim in [0, NJ)   # cols of B/E, rows of C/F, reduction dim in G
    k: dim in [0, NK)   # cols of A, rows of B (reduction for E)
    m: dim in [0, NM)   # cols of C, rows of D (reduction for F)
    l: dim in [0, NL)   # cols of D/F/G

data:
    # All matrices are stored in a single contiguous row-major block.
    # offset = row * leading_dimension + col

    A[i, k]: in DATA_TYPE
        = (i, k) -> i * NK + k           # NI x NK, row-major

    B[k, j]: in DATA_TYPE
        = (k, j) -> k * NJ + j           # NK x NJ, row-major

    C[j, m]: in DATA_TYPE
        = (j, m) -> j * NM + m           # NJ x NM, row-major

    D[m, l]: in DATA_TYPE
        = (m, l) -> m * NL + l           # NM x NL, row-major

    # E and F are logical intermediates.
    # In the baseline code they are fully materialized; in the optimized
    # model they may be partially or not materialized at all (see fusion
    # optimization), while preserving the final result G.
    E[i, j]: tmp DATA_TYPE
        = (i, j) -> i * NJ + j           # NI x NJ, row-major

    F[j, l]: tmp DATA_TYPE
        = (j, l) -> j * NL + l           # NJ x NL, row-major

    G[i, l]: out DATA_TYPE
        = (i, l) -> i * NL + l           # NI x NL, row-major

parameters:
    # Problem sizes (implicitly define the domain bounds)
    NI: int
    NJ: int
    NK: int
    NM: int
    NL: int

    # Tuning parameters for cache blocking; values should be chosen
    # according to the target machine (e.g., L1/L2 size, associativity).
    TI: int  # tile size along i (rows of A/E/G)
    TJ: int  # tile size along j (cols of B/E, rows of C/F)
    TK: int  # tile size along k (reduction for E)
    TM: int  # tile size along m (reduction for F)
    TL: int  # tile size along l (cols of D/F/G)

    # Vector widths for innermost loops (match SIMD width of hardware)
    VEC_J: int  # vector width when iterating j-contiguous data
    VEC_L: int  # vector width when iterating l-contiguous data

    # Unroll factors for reduction loops (small integers, e.g., 2,4,8)
    UNROLL_K: int  # for k in E
    UNROLL_M: int  # for m in F
    UNROLL_J: int  # for j reduction in G

    # Degree of threading (up to number of hardware threads)
    NUM_THREADS: int

computation:
    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. E := A * B   (NI x NK) * (NK x NJ) -> (NI x NJ)
    #     E[i, j] = sum_k A[i, k] * B[k, j]
    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    E_gemm:
        for i, j:
            E[i, j] = sum(k, A[i, k] * B[k, j])

    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. F := C * D   (NJ x NM) * (NM x NL) -> (NJ x NL)
    #     F[j, l] = sum_m C[j, m] * D[m, l]
    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    F_gemm:
        for j, l:
            F[j, l] = sum(m, C[j, m] * D[m, l])

    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. G := E * F   (NI x NJ) * (NJ x NL) -> (NI x NL)
    #     G[i, l] = sum_j E[i, j] * F[j, l]
    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    G_gemm:
        for i, l:
            G[i, l] = sum(j, E[i, j] * F[j, l])

dependencies:
    # E_gemm and F_gemm are completely independent.
    # G_gemm depends on the final values of both E and F.
    E_gemm -> G_gemm
    F_gemm -> G_gemm

optimization:
    #==================================================================
    # Cache blocking / tiling
    #==================================================================
    # Block all major dimensions to improve cache reuse.
    # The same symbolic tile sizes are reused across the three GEMMs.
    # This is semantically equivalent to the original loops; it only
    # changes the order of associative+commutative floating-point sums.

    # Tile "row" dimensions
    block(i, I, TI)   # I: tile index over rows of A, E, G
    block(j, J, TJ)   # J: tile index over NJ (cols of B/E, rows of C/F)
    block(l, L, TL)   # L: tile index over cols of D/F/G

    # Tile reduction dimensions
    block(k, K, TK)   # K: tile index over NK reduction in E_gemm
    block(m, M, TM)   # M: tile index over NM reduction in F_gemm

    # After blocking, the conceptual structure is:
    #
    #   E_gemm:
    #     for I in [0, NI) step TI
    #       for K in [0, NK) step TK
    #         for J in [0, NJ) step TJ
    #           for i in I-tile, k in K-tile, j in J-tile
    #             E[i, j] += A[i, k] * B[k, j]
    #
    #   F_gemm:
    #     for J in [0, NJ) step TJ
    #       for M in [0, NM) step TM
    #         for L in [0, NL) step TL
    #           for j in J-tile, m in M-tile, l in L-tile
    #             F[j, l] += C[j, m] * D[m, l]
    #
    #   G_gemm:
    #     for I in [0, NI) step TI
    #       for J in [0, NJ) step TJ
    #         for L in [0, NL) step TL
    #           for i in I-tile, j in J-tile, l in L-tile
    #             G[i, l] += E[i, j] * F[j, l]

    #==================================================================
    # Loop reordering for unit-stride access
    #==================================================================
    # Reorder loops inside each tile to maximize contiguous accesses.
    # Idea:
    #   - In E_gemm, use order (i, k, j):
    #       * A[i, k] traverses k contiguously (row of A).
    #       * B[k, j] traverses j contiguously (row of B).
    #       * E[i, j] traverses j contiguously (row of E).
    #
    #   - In F_gemm, use order (j, m, l):
    #       * C[j, m] traverses m contiguously (row of C).
    #       * D[m, l] traverses l contiguously (row of D).
    #       * F[j, l] traverses l contiguously (row of F).
    #
    #   - In G_gemm, use order (i, j, l):
    #       * E[i, j] traverses j contiguously (row of E).
    #       * F[j, l] traverses l contiguously (row of F).
    #       * G[i, l] traverses l contiguously (row of G).

    # These are implemented via loop interchange directives:
    interchange(j, k)   # in E_gemm: swap j and k to realize (i, k, j)
    interchange(l, m)   # in F_gemm: swap l and m to realize (j, m, l)
    interchange(l, j)   # in G_gemm: swap inner (j, l) to realize (i, j, l)

    #==================================================================
    # Parallelization
    #==================================================================
    # Use multi-core parallelism on the outer tiles; tile sizes TI, TJ, TL
    # should be large enough to give each thread a substantial chunk of work.

    # E_gemm: different I-tiles touch disjoint rows of E, so can be parallel.
    block(i, I_par, TI)
    parallelize(I_par)   # distribute I-tiles of E_gemm across threads

    # F_gemm: different J-tiles touch disjoint rows of F, so can be parallel.
    block(j, J_par, TJ)
    parallelize(J_par)   # distribute J-tiles of F_gemm across threads

    # G_gemm: again, rows of G are independent; parallelize over I-tiles.
    block(i, I_par_G, TI)
    parallelize(I_par_G)

    # NUM_THREADS controls the maximum concurrency; a runtime should choose
    # up to NUM_THREADS worker threads when scheduling parallel tiles.

    # Optional task-level parallelism:
    #   E_gemm and F_gemm are independent; they can run concurrently.
    #   G_gemm must start only after both complete, as expressed in
    #   the dependencies section.
    #
    #task_parallelize({E_gemm, F_gemm})
    #  # Custom directive:
    #  #   - Run E_gemm and F_gemm in separate parallel regions.
    #  #   - Respect E_gemm -> G_gemm and F_gemm -> G_gemm dependencies.

    #==================================================================
    # Vectorization and unrolling
    #==================================================================
    # Vectorize the innermost unit-stride loops over j or l.
    # VEC_J and VEC_L should match the hardware SIMD width for DATA_TYPE
    # (e.g., 4 for AVX2 double, 8 for AVX2 float, etc.).

    vectorize(j, VEC_J)   # innermost j-loops in E_gemm and G_gemm
    vectorize(l, VEC_L)   # innermost l-loops in F_gemm

    # Unroll reduction loops moderately to expose ILP and help the
    # compiler schedule FMA chains efficiently.
    unroll(k, UNROLL_K)   # reduction over k in E_gemm
    unroll(m, UNROLL_M)   # reduction over m in F_gemm
    unroll(j, UNROLL_J)   # reduction over j in G_gemm

    #==================================================================
    # Scalar replacement / register reuse
    #==================================================================
    # Within the reordered loops, hoist frequently used values into
    # scalars to minimize memory traffic. Conceptually:
    #
    #   - E_gemm inner kernel (within a tile):
    #       for i in I, for k in K:
    #           a_ik = A[i, k]              # hoist A[i,k]
    #           for j in J:
    #               E[i, j] += a_ik * B[k, j]
    #
    #   - F_gemm inner kernel:
    #       for j in J, for m in M:
    #           c_jm = C[j, m]              # hoist C[j,m]
    #           for l in L:
    #               F[j, l] += c_jm * D[m, l]
    #
    #   - G_gemm inner kernel:
    #       for i in I, for j in J:
    #           e_ij = E[i, j]              # hoist E[i,j]
    #           for l in L:
    #               G[i, l] += e_ij * F[j, l]
    #
    # A polyhedral or SSA-based optimizer should perform this scalar
    # replacement automatically once loop orders are as above.

    #==================================================================
    # Optional fusion to avoid fully materializing E
    #==================================================================
    # Since the program only observes G, E and F are intermediates.
    # It is legal (under the C "as-if" rule) to change the way they
    # are computed as long as G is unchanged.
    #
    # The most profitable fusion here is to avoid writing/reading E:
    #
    #   1. Compute F as before (F_gemm).
    #   2. Fuse E_gemm into G_gemm along the shared dimension j:
    #        for i in [0, NI):
    #          for l in [0, NL): G[i, l] = 0
    #          for j in [0, NJ):
    #            # compute e_ij on the fly (dot-product of row i of A
    #            # with column j of B)
    #            e_ij = sum(k, A[i, k] * B[k, j])
    #            # immediately consume e_ij into row i of G using
    #            # row j of F
    #            for l in [0, NL):
    #              G[i, l] += e_ij * F[j, l]
    #
    #   This preserves G exactly and reduces memory traffic by removing
    #   the large NI x NJ intermediate E.
    #
    # We express this as a high-level fusion directive:
    #
    #fuse(E_gemm, G_gemm, along = j)
    #  # Custom directive:
    #  #   - Replace the materialization of E with on-the-fly computation
    #  #     of e_ij inside G's accumulation over j.
    #  #   - Maintain all blocking, parallelization and vectorization
    #  #     structure on the (i, j, l, k) loops, now operating directly
    #  #     on A, B, F and G.
    #  #   - Does not increase asymptotic flop count and reduces memory
    #  #     footprint and bandwidth usage; extra temporaries are only
    #  #     scalar accumulators (e_ij), well within the 50% memory limit.

    # A similar but more aggressive fusion could also avoid full F
    # materialization by computing one or a few rows of F at a time into
    # a small buffer (size <= TL) and immediately consuming them in G.
    # Such buffers remain well below the 50% extra-memory budget.
--- END OF MODEL: 3mm-04 ---

    j: dim in [0, NJ)   # cols of B, E; rows of C, F; reduction index in G
    k: dim in [0, NK)   # cols of A; rows of B   (reduction index in E)

    B[k, j]: in DATA_TYPE
        = (k, j) -> k * NJ + j              # NK × NJ, row-major

    C[j, m]: in DATA_TYPE
        = (j, m) -> j * NM + m              # NJ × NM, row-major

    F[j, l]: inout DATA_TYPE

    G[i, l]: out DATA_TYPE
        = (i, l) -> i * NL + l              # NI × NL, row-major, final result

parameters:
    # Tuning parameters (constants, chosen for the target machine).

    # fits in L1/L2 cache; typical values on x64 (double) are 32–128.
    TI_E: int  # tile size for i in E = A*B
    TJ_E: int  # tile size for j in E = A*B
    TK_E: int  # tile size for k in E = A*B

    TJ_F: int  # tile size for j (row) in F = C*D
    TL_F: int  # tile size for l (col) in F = C*D
    TM_F: int  # tile size for m in F = C*D

    TI_G: int  # tile size for i in G = E*F
    TL_G: int  # tile size for l in G = E*F
    TJ_G: int  # tile size for j (reduction dim) in G = E*F

    VEC_E: int  # vectorization factor along j in E-phase (e.g., 8 for AVX-512 double)
    VEC_F: int  # vectorization factor along l in F-phase
    VEC_G: int  # vectorization factor along l in G-phase

    # E := A * B   (NI × NK) * (NK × NJ) → (NI × NJ)
    # Matches:
    #   for i in 0..NI-1
    #     for j in 0..NJ-1
    #       E[i][j] = 0;
    #       for k in 0..NK-1
    #         E[i][j] += A[i][k] * B[k][j];
    E_compute:
        for i in [0, NI), j in [0, NJ):
            E[i, j] = sum(k in [0, NK), A[i, k] * B[k, j])

    # F := C * D   (NJ × NM) * (NM × NL) → (NJ × NL)
    # Matches:
    #   for j in 0..NJ-1
    #     for l in 0..NL-1
    #       F[j][l] = 0;
    #       for m in 0..NM-1
    #         F[j][l] += C[j][m] * D[m][l];
    F_compute:
        for j in [0, NJ), l in [0, NL):
            F[j, l] = sum(m in [0, NM), C[j, m] * D[m, l])

    # Matches:
    #   for i in 0..NI-1
    #     for l in 0..NL-1
    #       G[i][l] = 0;
    #       for j in 0..NJ-1
    #         G[i][l] += E[i][j] * F[j][l];
    G_compute:
        for i in [0, NI), l in [0, NL):
            G[i, l] = sum(j in [0, NJ), E[i, j] * F[j, l])

    # E and F are independent and may be computed in any order or in parallel.

    F_compute -> G_compute

    # - All sums (sum(...)) are implemented as scalar reductions in
    #   registers to avoid repeated loads/stores of E, F, G elements.
    # - Parallelization is across output rows (i) so that each thread
    #   owns disjoint subsets of E/F/G and no synchronization is needed
    #   beyond the implicit barrier between phases.
    # - Blocking (tiling) is applied so that each inner kernel works on
    #   submatrices that fit in cache, increasing temporal locality.
    # - Vectorization targets the innermost, contiguous dimension in
    #   each kernel (j for E, l for F and G).
    #--------------------------------------------------------------

    #========================
    # 1) E = A * B  (NI × NK) * (NK × NJ)
    #========================
    # Base mathematical form:
    #   for i, j: E[i,j] = sum_k A[i,k] * B[k,j]
    # We transform loops to an i-k-j ordering with 3D blocking:
    #   for I_E in tiles of i
    #     for K_E in tiles of k
    #       for J_E in tiles of j
    #         for i inside I_E
    #           for k inside K_E
    #             a_ik = A[i,k]
    #             for j inside J_E
    #               E[i,j] += a_ik * B[k,j]
    #
    # This:
    #   - reuses A[i,k] across a block of columns j (register reuse)
    #   - accesses B[k,*] and E[i,*] contiguously along j
    #   - keeps each thread's writes to E disjoint when parallelizing over I_E.

    # Tile i, j, k for cache blocking
    block(i, I_E, TI_E)   # outer tile index I_E, inner i
    block(j, J_E, TJ_E)   # outer tile index J_E, inner j
    block(k, K_E, TK_E)   # outer tile index K_E, inner k

    # Hoist tile loops outward: I_E outermost, then K_E, then J_E.
    # (Exact nesting: I_E -> K_E -> J_E -> i -> k -> j)
    hoist(I_E)
    hoist(K_E)
    hoist(J_E)

    # Interchange original j and k loops inside each (i,⋅) band:
    # original: for j: for k:
    # desired:  for k: for j:
    interchange(j, k)

    # Parallelize over row tiles of E (I_E); each thread updates
    # disjoint rows of E, reading shared A and B.
    parallelize(I_E)

    # Vectorize innermost j loop over contiguous columns of E and B.
    vectorize(j, VEC_E)

    # Optionally unroll the inner k loop modestly to improve ILP.
    unroll(k, 4)

    #========================
    # 2) F = C * D  (NJ × NM) * (NM × NL)
    #========================
    # Mathematical form:
    #   for j, l: F[j,l] = sum_m C[j,m] * D[m,l]
    # Apply analogous i-k-j pattern with indices (j,m,l):
    #   for J_F in tiles of j
    #     for M_F in tiles of m
    #       for L_F in tiles of l
    #         for j in J_F
    #           for m in M_F
    #             c_jm = C[j,m]
    #             for l in L_F
    #               F[j,l] += c_jm * D[m,l]
    #
    # This keeps C[j,*] and F[j,*]/D[m,*] accesses contiguous in l in
    # the innermost loop and allows parallelism over j-tiles.

    block(j, J_F, TJ_F)   # tile rows of F/C
    block(m, M_F, TM_F)   # tile inner reduction dim
    block(l, L_F, TL_F)   # tile columns of F/D

    hoist(J_F)
    hoist(M_F)
    hoist(L_F)

    # Interchange original l and m loops so m becomes middle and l innermost:
    interchange(l, m)

    # Parallelize over J_F (row tiles of F).
    parallelize(J_F)

    # Vectorize innermost l loop over contiguous columns of F and D.
    vectorize(l, VEC_F)

    unroll(m, 4)

    #========================
    # 3) G = E * F  (NI × NJ) * (NJ × NL)
    #========================
    # Mathematical form:
    #   for i, l: G[i,l] = sum_j E[i,j] * F[j,l]
    #
    # Reorder to accumulate G row by row, iterating over j (reduction)
    # in the middle and l as the innermost contiguous dimension:
    #   for I_G in tiles of i
    #     for J_G in tiles of j
    #       for L_G in tiles of l
    #         for i in I_G
    #           for j in J_G
    #             e_ij = E[i,j]
    #             for l in L_G
    #               G[i,l] += e_ij * F[j,l]
    #
    # This:
    #   - keeps G[i,*] and F[j,*] accesses contiguous in l
    #   - reuses e_ij across a block of columns l
    #   - respects the reduction over j (J_G and j remain sequential)
    #   - allows safe parallelization over row tiles I_G.

    block(i, I_G, TI_G)
    block(j, J_G, TJ_G)
    block(l, L_G, TL_G)

    hoist(I_G)
    hoist(J_G)
    hoist(L_G)

    # Interchange l (original second loop) with j (reduction) so
    # that inside each (i, J_G) band we use i-j-l ordering.
    interchange(l, j)

    # Parallelize over row tiles of G.
    parallelize(I_G)

    # Vectorize innermost l loop over contiguous columns of G and F.
    vectorize(l, VEC_G)

    unroll(j, 4)

    #--------------------------------------------------------------
    # Optional advanced optimization (commented, semantics-preserving)
    #--------------------------------------------------------------
    # #block(j, J_COMMON, TJ_G)
    # # 3-way blocking in the shared NJ dimension:
    # #   for each j-tile J_COMMON:
    # #     - compute the corresponding slice E[:,J_COMMON] from A,B
    # #     - compute the corresponding slice F[J_COMMON,:] from C,D
    # #     - update G using only these slices

#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */
#include "3mm.h"


/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array(int ni, int nj, int nk, int nl, int nm,
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,NI,NK,ni,nk),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(B,NK,NJ,nk,nj),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(C,NJ,NM,nj,nm),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(D,NM,NL,nm,nl))
{
  int i, j;

  for (i = 0; i < ni; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < nk; j++)
      A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) ((i*j+1) % ni) / (5*ni);
  for (i = 0; i < nk; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < nj; j++)
      B[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) ((i*(j+1)+2) % nj) / (5*nj);
  for (i = 0; i < nj; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < nm; j++)
      C[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) (i*(j+3) % nl) / (5*nl);
  for (i = 0; i < nm; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < nl; j++)
      D[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) ((i*(j+2)+2) % nk) / (5*nk);
}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int ni, int nl,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(G,NI,NL,ni,nl))
{
  int i, j;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("G");
  for (i = 0; i < ni; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < nl; j++) {
	if ((i * ni + j) % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
	fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, G[i][j]);
    }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("G");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_3mm[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int ni, int nj, int nk, int nl, int nm,
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(E,NI,NJ,ni,nj),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,NI,NK,ni,nk),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(B,NK,NJ,nk,nj),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(F,NJ,NL,nj,nl),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(C,NJ,NM,nj,nm),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(D,NM,NL,nm,nl),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(G,NI,NL,ni,nl))
{
  int i, j, k;

#pragma scop
  /* E := A*B */
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_NI; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < _PB_NJ; j++)
      {
	E[i][j] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0);
	for (k = 0; k < _PB_NK; ++k)
	  E[i][j] += A[i][k] * B[k][j];
      }
  /* F := C*D */
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_NJ; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < _PB_NL; j++)
      {
	F[i][j] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0);
	for (k = 0; k < _PB_NM; ++k)
	  F[i][j] += C[i][k] * D[k][j];
      }
  /* G := E*F */
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_NI; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < _PB_NL; j++)
      {
	G[i][j] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0);
	for (k = 0; k < _PB_NJ; ++k)
	  G[i][j] += E[i][k] * F[k][j];
      }
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int ni = NI;
  int nj = NJ;
  int nk = NK;
  int nl = NL;
  int nm = NM;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(E, DATA_TYPE, NI, NJ, ni, nj);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(A, DATA_TYPE, NI, NK, ni, nk);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(B, DATA_TYPE, NK, NJ, nk, nj);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(F, DATA_TYPE, NJ, NL, nj, nl);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(C, DATA_TYPE, NJ, NM, nj, nm);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(D, DATA_TYPE, NM, NL, nm, nl);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(G, DATA_TYPE, NI, NL, ni, nl);

  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (ni, nj, nk, nl, nm,
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(C),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(D));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_3mm (ni, nj, nk, nl, nm,
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(E),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(F),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(C),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(D),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(G));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(ni, nl,  POLYBENCH_ARRAY(G)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(E);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(B);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(F);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(C);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(D);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(G);

  return 0;
}

parameters:
    # Problem sizes (modeled as parameters, but compile-time constants in PolyBench)
    NI: int
    NJ: int
    NK: int
    NL: int
    NM: int

    # Tunable tile sizes (chosen for cache hierarchy of the target system)
    TI_E: int  # tile size for i in E = A * B
    TJ_E: int  # tile size for j in E = A * B
    TK_E: int  # tile size for k in E = A * B

    TJ_F: int  # tile size for j in F = C * D
    TL_F: int  # tile size for l in F = C * D
    TM_F: int  # tile size for m in F = C * D

    TI_G: int  # tile size for i in G = E * F
    TL_G: int  # tile size for l in G = E * F
    TJ_G: int  # tile size for j (reduction dim) in G = E * F

    VEC:  int  # SIMD vector length in elements (e.g., 4/8 for double; 8/16 for float)

computation:
    # Phase 1: E := A * B   (NI x NJ  =  NI x NK  *  NK x NJ)
    E_phase:
        for i, j:
            E[i, j] = sum(k, A[i, k] * B[k, j])

    # Phase 2: F := C * D   (NJ x NL  =  NJ x NM  *  NM x NL)
    F_phase:
        for j, l:
            F[j, l] = sum(m, C[j, m] * D[m, l])

    # Phase 3: G := E * F   (NI x NL  =  NI x NJ  *  NJ x NL)
    G_phase:
        for i, l:
            G[i, l] = sum(j, E[i, j] * F[j, l])

dependencies:
    # E and F are independent; G depends on both.
    E_phase -> G_phase
    F_phase -> G_phase

optimization:
    # ==========================================================
    # General strategy
    # ==========================================================
    # - Keep the reduction index innermost in each GEMM, so that:
    #     * left operand uses row-major layout with contiguous access
    #     * right operand uses column-major layout with contiguous access
    #   This makes the innermost loop a vectorizable dot product.
    # - Tile the (row, col, reduction) dimensions to improve cache reuse.
    # - Use outer tiles for parallelization across cores.
    # - Use scalar accumulators per output element within tiles to minimize
    #   memory traffic (read/write E, F, G only once per tile).
    # - Optional packing for B, D, F tiles keeps packed buffers small enough
    #   that added memory is well below +50% of the original footprint.

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # Phase 1: E = A * B
    # Loop shape after transformation:
    #
    # for iE in 0..NI step TI_E         # tiled, parallel
    #   for jE in 0..NJ step TJ_E
    #     for kE in 0..NK step TK_E
    #       for i in iE .. min(iE+TI_E, NI)
    #         for j in jE .. min(jE+TJ_E, NJ)
    #           acc = (kE == 0 ? 0 : E[i,j])
    #           for k in kE .. min(kE+TK_E, NK)   # contiguous A[i,k] and B[k,j]
    #             acc += A[i,k] * B[k,j]
    #           E[i,j] = acc
    #
    block(i, iE, TI_E)             # tile over rows of A/E
    block(j, jE, TJ_E)             # tile over cols of B/E
    block(k, kE, TK_E)             # tile over reduction dimension
    hoist(iE)                      # make tile loops outermost: iE, jE, kE
    hoist(jE)
    hoist(kE)
    parallelize(iE)                # distribute row-tiles across threads
    vectorize(k, VEC)              # vectorize dot product over k
    unroll(k, 4)                   # unroll for ILP within a SIMD chunk

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # Phase 2: F = C * D
    # Similar tiling over (j, l, m), j-tiles in parallel.
    #
    # for jF in 0..NJ step TJ_F      # tiled, parallel (rows of C/F)
    #   for lF in 0..NL step TL_F
    #     for mF in 0..NM step TM_F
    #       for j in jF .. min(jF+TJ_F, NJ)
    #         for l in lF .. min(lF+TL_F, NL)
    #           acc = (mF == 0 ? 0 : F[j,l]
    #           for m in mF .. min(mF+TM_F, NM)   # contiguous C[j,m], D[m,l]
    #             acc += C[j,m] * D[m,l]
    #           F[j,l] = acc
    #
    block(j, jF, TJ_F)             # tile rows of C/F
    block(l, lF, TL_F)             # tile cols of D/F
    block(m, mF, TM_F)             # tile reduction dimension
    hoist(jF)
    hoist(lF)
    hoist(mF)
    parallelize(jF)                # distribute row-tiles across threads
    vectorize(m, VEC)              # vectorize dot product over m
    unroll(m, 4)

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # Phase 3: G = E * F
    # Tiling and parallelization over (i, l, j). j is reduction dim.
    #
    # for iG in 0..NI step TI_G      # tiled, parallel (rows of E/G)
    #   for lG in 0..NL step TL_G
    #     for jG in 0..NJ step TJ_G
    #       for i in iG .. min(iG+TI_G, NI)
    #         for l in lG .. min(lG+TL_G, NL)
    #           acc = (jG == 0 ? 0 : G[i,l])
    #           for j in jG .. min(jG+TJ_G, NJ)   # contiguous E[i,j], F[j,l]
    #             acc += E[i,j] * F[j,l]
    #           G[i,l] = acc
    #
    block(i, iG, TI_G)             # tile rows of E/G
    block(l, lG, TL_G)             # tile cols of F/G
    block(j, jG, TJ_G)             # tile reduction dimension
    hoist(iG)
    hoist(lG)
    hoist(jG)
    parallelize(iG)                # distribute row-tiles across threads
    vectorize(j, VEC)              # vectorize dot product over j
    unroll(j, 4)

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # Data layout and packing
    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # The data section already specifies B, D, and F as column-major, so an
    # implementation should either:
    #   - allocate them directly in that layout, or
    #   - pack tiles on the fly into small contiguous buffers.
    #
    # Below are non-standard directives describing per-tile packing.
    #
    # pack(M, [rdim, cdim], [Rtile, Ctile]) means:
    #   For each (Rtile, Ctile) tile of matrix M, allocate a temporary buffer
    #   of size (tile_size(rdim) x tile_size(cdim)) and copy M's elements into
    #   a layout where 'rdim' is contiguous. Buffers are reused across tiles,
    #   and their total size is O(T* T) per thread, far below 50% overhead.
    #
    pack(B, [k, j], [kE, jE])      # pack B tiles for better use of L1/L2
    pack(D, [m, l], [mF, lF])      # similarly for D
    pack(F, [j, l], [jG, lG])      # optional: pack F tiles for phase 3

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # Task parallelism between independent phases
    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # E_phase and F_phase are independent; they can be run as separate tasks
    # sharing a thread pool. G_phase starts after both complete.
    #
    # Non-standard directives:
    #   task_parallel(L1, L2, ...) : run labeled computations as concurrent tasks
    #   task_sync(L)               : L can start only after all prior tasks finish
    #
    task_parallel(E_phase, F_phase)
    task_sync(G_phase)
--- END OF MODEL: 3mm-02 ---
